Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1 (2024-09-10)
- History: Prices declining from 72.11 to 66.52 over 18 days (about 8% decline)
- Sentiment: Starts at 0.67, ends at 0.67, with some variation
- Model forecast (30-day): Starts at 65.06, gradually increases to 68.49
- True outcome: Starts at 64.92, gradually increases to 61.76

Looking at the difference:
- At day 1: Model 65.06 vs True 64.92 (0.04 difference, very close)
- At day 10: Model 67.35 vs True 64.10 (3.25 difference)
- At day 20: Model 63.58 vs True 60.29 (3.29 difference)

Wait, let me look more carefully. The model seems to be under-predicting (model lower than true) in most cases, especially in the latter half of the 30-day horizon.

Actually, looking at this more carefully:
- The history shows prices were declining from ~72 to ~66.5
- But the true outcome continues declining to ~61.8
- The model predicts a floor around 65-68

Let me look at the other examples to find patterns.

## Example 2 (2023-12-20)
- History: Prices oscillating around 70-76
- Sentiment: Mix of positive, zero, and negative (-1.00)
- Model forecast: Starts at 75.29, ends at 71.34
- True outcome: Starts at 75.36, ends at 63.50

The model significantly over-predicts compared to the true outcome. The true outcome drops much more than expected - falling from 75.36 to 63.50 (about 16%), while the model only falls to 71.34 (about 6% from start).

Sentiment seems to play a complex role, with the model struggling to accurately predict price movements, especially during declining trends.
